text: WhatsApp from +91-98XXX-XXXXX: 'Hi! Earn ₹8,000/day from home! Just rate 5-star reviews for Amazon products. Reply YES to start earning TODAY! No experience needed!'
tells: upfront promise of high daily earnings for trivial tasks
no company name or verifiable details

text: Email from placements.northridge-institute.org.in, Subject: Placement Drive — Vertex Dynamics (₹6.5 LPA): 'Dear student, congratulations! You've been shortlisted for the final round. tells: sender domain is a lookalike of your institute's real domain
fee demanded to 'confirm' a placement slot
real campus placements never charge students registration fees
safe_action: Do not pay; confirm the drive with your institute's official placement office in person or via the official portal.

text: Facebook ad comment reply: 'Want to work in Canada? 100% GUARANTEED work permit in 30 days! No IELTS needed! Pay only ₹45,000 advance. DM me now — only 10 slots left!'
tells: guarantees a government work permit — no agent can do that
'no IELTS needed' for Canadian work migration is false
safe_action: Ignore; real immigration routes are listed on the official Government of Canada website. Never pay advances to social-media agents.

text: Email, Subject: Mystery Shopper Assignment — ₹3,500 per visit + expenses: 'Hello! RetailAudit India has selected you as a mystery shopper. We will courier you a cheque of ₹28,000 for your first assignment: cash ₹20,000, keep ₹3,500 as your fee, and wire the rest to our vendor for the product test. Start this week!'
tells: advance cheque that you'll be asked to cash and forward most of — classic fake-cheque scam
overpayment + 'wire the rest' is the core fraud pattern
no verifiable company details or website
safe_action: Do not accept or cash the cheque. Cheque fraud leaves YOU liable when it bounces. Report to cybercrime.gov.in.

text: Instagram DM from @starline_castings: 'Hi! We're casting junior artists & assistant crew for a big OTT web series shooting in Mumbai next month. Pay ₹50,000–₹70,000 per project. To block your slot, pay ₹2,500 artist-registration fee via UPI. Limited seats!'
tells: upfront registration fee to 'block' a job slot
casting via Instagram DM from an unverifiable handle
vague 'big OTT series' with no production name
safe_action: Legitimate productions never charge to hire you. Verify through established casting agencies or the production house directly.

text: Email, Subject: Volunteer Coordinator Role — Sahyog Foundation: 'Dear applicant, we're impressed by your profile. As discussed, the field-volunteer role includes a stipend of ₹12,000/month. Before onboarding, all volunteers complete a mandatory 2-day orientation (₹1,800 training fee, receipt provided). Reply to confirm your batch.'
tells: fee charged to the volunteer before any work begins
real NGOs don't charge volunteers orientation fees
safe_action: Verify the NGO's registration (NGO Darpan / 80G) independently and visit their office; never pay to volunteer.

text: LinkedIn message from 'Aarav Kapoor, HR — Zenith Capital Markets': 'Your profile fits our Junior Forex Analyst role (WFH, ₹80,000/month + bonuses). First step: open a demo trading account with our partner broker using the link below and complete the practice module.'
tells: job interview conducted entirely over LinkedIn chat
asks you to open a broker account via their referral link before any interview
likely an affiliate-commission funnel, not a real job
safe_action: Do not open accounts via their links. Real employers interview you first; check the company on MCA/regulatory records.

text: Telegram message: 'RENT YOUR UPI ACCOUNT! Earn ₹10,000/month doing NOTHING. We just need your PhonePe/GPay for business payments. 100% legal, 100% safe. DM now!'
tells: renting your bank/UPI account to strangers is money-mule recruitment
accounts used this way route fraud proceeds — a criminal offence
safe_action: Never rent or share your bank/UPI account. If you already did, inform your bank and the police immediately.

Regards, Talent Acquisition'

no prior application or shortlist notice
generic venue details that can't be verified
safe_action: Cross-check the drive with your placement cell and the company's official careers page before attending.

tells: asks for passport copy + instalment payments over WhatsApp
unregistered consultancy with no verifiable licence number
safe_action: Check MARA registration for Australia agents; never share passport copies over WhatsApp.

payment promised before any verified company identity
no company website, registration, or physical address given
safe_action: Verify the company exists (business registry, real domain, phone). Never sign or return documents with personal ID details.

tells: 'friend of a friend' framing to lower suspicion
your account would receive and forward crypto-scam proceeds
high per-transaction payout for doing nothing = money laundering

no verifiable case number on any official immigration portal
safe_action: Check your application status only on the country's official immigration website. Never pay via agent escrow.

UPI payment to a personal handle

polite, professional tone masks advance-fee pattern

unsolicited contact with knowledge of your loss

text: Heyy! Okay I know this is forward but your third photo — the one at the café with the book — I literally stopped mid-scroll 😅 I'm Arjun, 29, architect in Pune. I don't usually message first but something about your profile felt... familiar? Like we've met in another life. Would love to actually get to know you properly. Coffee's on me ☕
tells: instant intense interest after zero interaction
safe_action: Enjoy the chat but keep the pace slow; don't move off the app or share personal details until you've verified they're real.

text: Good morning ☀️ I know we've only been talking for two days but I need to be honest with you — I've never felt this kind of connection with anyone. You just... get me. My friends think I'm crazy. Maybe I am. But I can't stop thinking about our conversation last night. — Vikram
tells: love-bombing after only 2 days of contact
safe_action: Scammers rush emotional bonding to create obligation; keep the pace realistic and share nothing personal or financial.

text: haha I'd love to video call, honestly, but my front camera cracked last week and I haven't fixed it yet 🙈 Can we just keep talking here? Your voice notes are enough for me tbh. You have such a calming voice.
tells: refuses video verification with a convenient excuse
keeps relationship text-only where identity can't be checked
safe_action: A persistent refusal to video call is a major red flag; insist on a live call before trusting the relationship.

text: Yeah so I'm a subsea engineer — I work 6 weeks on, 3 off on a rig off the Malaysian coast. Signal is patchy, sometimes I go quiet for days, please don't take it personally 🙏 The money's good but honestly it's lonely out here. That's why meeting someone like you means a lot. When I'm back on rotation in December, I'd love to fly to you.
tells: classic offshore persona that explains long absences
future in-person promise keeps victim invested without ever happening
safe_action: Offshore/rig stories are textbook romance-scam setups; verify identity with a live video call before believing any of it.

text: Good morning beautiful 🌹 Did you sleep well? I woke up thinking about you. Have an amazing day — text me when you're free, I miss our chats already 💭
tells: pet names within days of matching
safe_action: Intense daily romantic messaging this early is grooming, not romance; slow down and watch for inconsistencies.

text: I'm currently deployed — peacekeeping rotation, can't say exactly where. We get limited phone time and no video calls allowed (operational security). I know it's a lot to ask, but please be patient with me. You remind me of home, and that keeps me going.
tells: military persona justifying zero video contact
emotional leverage ('you keep me going') to discourage questions
safe_action: Real service members can usually video call; 'no video ever allowed' plus secrecy is a classic scam script.

text: I'm a crypto trader, mostly BTC and ETH — I do pretty well for myself, retired my parents last year. Not bragging, just saying I value financial freedom. Actually if you're ever curious I could show you how it works, it's simpler than people think 📈 But no pressure at all, I like you for you.
tells: wealth signaling sets up a future investment pitch
soft offer to 'teach' trading is grooming for pig-butchering
safe_action: Wealth talk early in dating often sets up an investment scam; never send money or invest on a romantic partner's advice.

text: I lost my wife three years ago. It's taken me a long time to even open this app. My daughter Aisha is 8 — she's the light of my life. I don't want to rush anything... but talking to you feels like the first real thing since. Please be honest with me, that's all I ask.
tells: emotional vulnerability used to accelerate trust
asks for honesty while the persona itself is unverifiable
safe_action: Grief stories that arrive within days are designed to bond you fast; verify the person's identity independently.

text: [Profile bio: Arjun, 30 — lives in Mumbai] | Message: Ugh, my commute is killing me — Gurgaon to South Delhi every day 😩 Anyway how was your day? Did that presentation go well?
tells: profile says Mumbai but the commute is Gurgaon to South Delhi — location contradiction
scammers juggle multiple scripts and slip on details like this
safe_action: Note contradictions; scammers juggle multiple scripts. Ask casual clarifying questions and watch for deflection.

text: I'm an orthopedic surgeon, but I also trained as a chef (long story 😄), I volunteer at an animal shelter on Sundays, I speak three languages, and I'm training for a marathon. My friends say I'm 'too much' lol. What about you — what's your story?
tells: designed to impress on every dimension at once
safe_action: Nobody is a surgeon-chef-polyglot-marathoner-volunteer; too-perfect profiles are assembled to dazzle, not to be real.

text: I'm more of a texter tbh... my flatmate is always around and I get shy lol. Your messages are enough 💌
safe_action: Someone who will never voice-call after weeks of 'deep connection' is hiding their identity; insist on a live call.

text: Hey, I barely check this app — I'm much more active on WhatsApp. It's +91-98XXX-XXXXX. Message me there? I hate losing good conversations to this app's notifications 😅
tells: tries to move conversation off the moderated platform within days
safe_action: Stay on the dating app until trust is established; moving off-app early is a classic scammer move.

text: I already told my mom about you 😳 She saw me smiling at my phone. It's only been 3 days and I feel like I've known you forever. Is that crazy?
tells: fake family involvement to seem serious
safe_action: Declaring family-level seriousness after 3 days is love-bombing; real relationships don't run on fast-forward.

text: Boarding in 20 — Dubai to Singapore ✈️ I'll be radio silent for ~8 hours, then a 2-day layover. Hate this part. Wish you were in the seat next to me. Text you when I land, promise.
safe_action: Perpetual travel that always blocks meeting in person is a setup; suggest a video call during a layover.

text: Here's me last weekend 📸 Took this myself — well, my tripod did lol. I do wedding photography, so I'm usually behind the camera!
tells: professional-quality photos inconsistent with a casual selfie claim
safe_action: Reverse-image-search profile photos; scammers routinely use stolen model or stock shots.

text: Contracts here are insane — just signed one worth more than my house back home lol. Money's not everything though. Honestly I'd trade it all for someone real. That's why I'm here, not on some yacht.
tells: frames wealth as irrelevant to disarm skepticism
safe_action: Flashing big contracts while claiming money doesn't matter is designed to impress and lower your guard.

text: I've never met anyone like you. Everyone else on this app feels so shallow, but you — you're different. I can feel it.
safe_action: Being told you're uniquely special by a stranger is flattery as a tactic; enjoy it, but verify who they are.

text: I'm leading the design on a resort project in the Maldives — 14 months on-site. It's paradise but lonely. The renders look amazing though, I'll show you sometime. Maybe you'll visit when it's done 😉
safe_action: A 14-month remote posting that conveniently prevents meeting is a common script; ask for a live video call.

text: I'm not on Instagram or anything — deleted all social media last year, best decision ever. I like keeping life private, you know?
tells: frames secrecy as a lifestyle choice
safe_action: No social presence plus no video calls means zero verifiable identity; treat the persona as unproven.

text: I'm with a medical NGO near the border — signal is terrible, and video calls are basically impossible here. If I go quiet, I'm probably in surgery. Just know I'm thinking of you.
tells: medical emergencies as cover for silence
safe_action: Noble-job stories that make verification 'impossible' are a red flag; real aid workers can usually manage a call.

text: I'm a jewelry designer 💍 I keep picturing a piece I'd make for you — something delicate, with a stone that matches your eyes. One day, maybe.
safe_action: Lavish gift fantasies early on are grooming; don't share your address or personal details for 'surprises'.

text: Forex is wild — had a green week, up nicely 📊 I don't talk numbers on here though, people get weird about money. Let's just say I'm comfortable. What matters is finding someone genuine.
tells: trading success hinted at while details withheld to seem modest
positions as a future mentor figure
safe_action: Hints of trading wealth in a dating chat are usually the runway to an investment pitch; don't follow it.

text: Can we delete this app? I only downloaded it to find you 😌 I don't want to keep swiping. Let's just talk here, it's more... us.
tells: isolation tactic — removes victim from the moderated platform
romantic framing of a control move
safe_action: Deleting the app 'for us' cuts off reporting and safety tools; keep chatting where you matched.

text: On sabbatical in Lisbon this semester — the timezone thing is annoying, sorry if I reply at odd hours! Teaching's on pause so I'm writing a book. Would love a reader with good taste 😉
tells: timezone excuse for odd-hour replies (script-farming pattern)
safe_action: Odd-hours messaging blamed on timezones fits scammers working multiple targets; verify with a live call.

text: I miss you. I know we only started talking yesterday, but I already miss you when you're offline. Is that weird? Don't answer that 😅
tells: 'I miss you' after one day of chatting
safe_action: Missing someone you met yesterday isn't romance, it's a pressure tactic; keep emotional distance early on.

text: Satellite phone only out here, and calls cost a fortune, so I mostly text. 4 more weeks on this rotation. Counting the days till I'm back on land — and till I can finally hear your voice properly.
tells: communication limits baked into the persona
safe_action: Every excuse delays the one thing that would prove they're real: a live call. Insist on it.

text: You mentioned your dad runs a business — that's amazing! Are you close with your family? I love that. Family is everything to me ❤️ What do your parents do?
safe_action: Fast, detailed questions about family and finances are reconnaissance; share personal details slowly.

text: Closing a big deal next week — 40-unit project. Fingers crossed 🤞 If it goes through I'm taking a month off. Maybe we finally meet then. I want our first meeting to be perfect.
tells: big-deal story sets up a future 'need help with funds' twist
meeting is perpetually one deal away
safe_action: The 'one big deal then we meet' pattern keeps you hooked; don't send money for any deal-related emergency.

text: Everyone here just wants hookups. You're the first person I've actually wanted to talk to past midnight about real things.
safe_action: Being cast as 'the only real one' is flattering by design; stay grounded and verify identity.

text: I do private security contracting — most of what I do I can't talk about, hope you understand. No video calls, ever — company policy with the clients I have. It's not that I don't want to see you.
tells: preemptive permanent excuse for no video
safe_action: 'No video calls, ever' is not a job requirement, it's a scammer's shield; walk away from unverifiable personas.

text: If we ever got a place together I'd do the interiors myself — warm minimalism, lots of plants, a reading nook for you 📚 Sorry, I'm getting ahead of myself lol. But I can picture it.
tells: domestic future-faking after a short acquaintance
safe_action: Planning 'our apartment' with someone you just met is future-faking to deepen attachment; keep it in the present.

text: I got into crypto early — 2017. Life-changing, honestly. I don't flaunt it. Most people here wouldn't understand the discipline it took. You seem smarter than that.
tells: positions as a mentor figure for a future pitch
safe_action: Early-crypto wealth stories in dating chats are usually the setup for pig-butchering; never invest via a romantic contact.

text: Enough about me 😄 — I want to know everything about YOU. What's your biggest dream? Like, the real one.
tells: keeps focus on the victim to harvest information
safe_action: Someone who never answers anything about themselves while mining your life story is running a script.

text: After my wife passed, I promised her I'd find happiness again — she'd want that. My therapist says I'm ready. I think meeting you is... I don't know. A sign? Sorry, too much too soon.
safe_action: Weaponized grief that arrives within days is designed to bond you; verify identity before investing emotionally.

text: Roses are red, but they fade with time / your smile, though, outshines... okay I'm bad at this 😂 But seriously, not a morning goes by that I don't think of you first. 🌅💛🌹
safe_action: Daily poetry-level intensity from a near-stranger is grooming rhythm; match their energy with caution.

text: Layover in Frankfurt — 26 hours. This job: great views, terrible for relationships. Every captain I know is divorced lol. Trying to do things differently this time. You make me want to.
tells: sympathy plus 'you're my reason to change' framing
safe_action: The 'you make me want to be better' line creates emotional responsibility; don't let it rush trust.

text: I told my sister about you — showed her your photo (hope that's okay 😅). She said 'finally, he found someone normal' lol. No pressure though!
tells: fake social proof via invented third parties
safe_action: Invented family members who 'approve of you' make the fantasy feel real; it's still unverified.

text: I manage portfolios for a living, so forgive me — I notice you keep your savings in a regular savings account? No judgment! Just... there's so much more your money could be doing. Happy to look at it sometime, pro bono 😉
tells: positions for a future fund-access request
still framed as helpful, not an ask
safe_action: A romantic interest offering to 'look at' your savings is the soft opening of an investment scam; decline firmly.

text: lol I'm 32 — wait did I say 34 before? I'm 32, turning 33 in March. Ugh, I can never keep track 😅
tells: sign of a scripted or multi-target operation
safe_action: Small contradictions reveal a persona, not a person; confront gently and watch how they recover.

text: Banking here is a nightmare — transfers take weeks and the fees are criminal. I mostly get paid in cash allowances. It's fine, you adapt. Anyway, tell me about your day — I live for your messages out here.
tells: 'banking is complicated here' plants the seed for a future money-movement request
safe_action: Banking-trouble stories are the classic prelude to 'can you receive money for me'; never agree to move funds.

text: Goodnight my queen 👑 Dream of me, okay? You're the last thought on my mind tonight. Every night, actually.
tells: intense pet names within days of matching
safe_action: 'My queen' on day three is love-bombing, not devotion; keep perspective on the timeline.

text: We're mid-Pacific, 11 more days to port. No signal most days — I write you messages and they all send at once when we get coverage, sorry if it's a flood 😅⛵
tells: message-burst pattern explained away by the persona
unreachable for months at a time
safe_action: Burst messaging blamed on 'no signal' fits mass-scripting; a real person finds a way to video call in port.

text: Be honest — are you talking to other people on here? I just... I feel like what we have is different and the thought of you with someone else drives me crazy.
safe_action: Jealousy this early is about control, not love; healthy interest doesn't interrogate you in week one.

text: We're closing our seed round — oversubscribed, actually. Wild year. I don't usually date during fundraise season but you're worth making time for. Investors love my 'story' lol.
safe_action: Founder-status flexing is designed to impress; status claims are cheap, video calls are not — ask for one.

text: This song came on and I immediately thought of you 🎶 Listen to the lyrics — that's exactly how I feel. It's only been a week and you've rewired my brain lol.
tells: accelerated attachment claims after one week
safe_action: 'You've rewired my brain' after a week is intensity as strategy; let real time do the bonding.

text: I'm in Bangkok for the gem expo — picked up something beautiful today. Not telling what 😉 Let's just say someone's getting spoiled when I visit. I love surprising people I care about.
tells: gift promise sets up a future 'customs fee, please help' twist
safe_action: Gift promises reliably precede 'the parcel is stuck, please pay the fee'; never pay fees for a stranger's gift.

text: My friends say I NEVER do this — I'm usually so guarded. But with you my walls just... came down. Don't break my heart, okay? 🥺
safe_action: 'Don't break my heart' this early manufactures obligation; real vulnerability takes time.

text: 6-month contract on a cruise liner — the infirmary is quiet most days, thank god. Satellite wifi is expensive so I ration it. Your messages are what I spend it on, worth every rupee 😊
tells: rationed contact built into the story
flattery keeps the victim waiting patiently
safe_action: Expensive-wifi stories justify minimal contact while maximizing emotional output; verify in person or by video.

text: Two messages in and I already know — this is fate. I don't believe in coincidences. The universe put you on my screen for a reason. ✨
safe_action: Fate-talk after two messages is a script, not a soulmate; slow the conversation down.

text: I want to send you something — nothing big, just a little surprise 🎁 What's your address? And your full name for the courier? I love giving gifts, it's my love language.
tells: requests home address plus full name very early
personal data harvesting framed as romance
safe_action: Never share your home address with someone you haven't video-verified; 'surprises' are a data-harvesting pretext.

text: FINAL NOTICE: Your car warranty expires in 7 days. You have ignored our previous notices. Call 1800-xxx-xxxx now to extend coverage before it's too late. — Vehicle Protection Dept
tells: generic sender with no vehicle identified
safe_action: Treat as suspicious until verified: real warranty offers come from your dealer or manufacturer — confirm there, never via this message.

text:
Subject: Invoice #INV-88412 — payment due

Dear Sir/Madam,

Please find attached invoice for Rs 18,450 for facility services rendered. Payment is due within 48 hours to avoid late fees.

Regards,
Brightline Facility Services
tells: unsolicited invoice from an unknown vendor
safe_action: Treat as suspicious until verified: check with your accounts team whether this vendor exists and services were received.

text: Hi, I'm Priya from TalentEdge HR. Your profile stood out. We have a remote Data Analyst role, Rs 80k/month. Initial screening happens on Telegram — message @talentedge_hr with code TE-221. Quick process!
safe_action: Treat as suspicious until verified: real recruiters interview on official channels — confirm the company and role on LinkedIn first.

text: Bro trust me, my cousin doubled his money in 3 weeks on this platform. I'm putting 50k in. Link below, use my referral code and we both get a bonus. Don't sleep on this 🚀
safe_action: Treat as suspicious until verified: 'doubled in 3 weeks' is a classic pig-butchering hook — research the platform independently.

text: Aarav, 6, needs heart surgery in 72 HOURS or he won't make it. 💔 Every minute counts. Donate now: [shortlink]. 80G receipt available. Please share — his life is in your hands.
tells: donation via shortlink, not a known NGO site
safe_action: Treat as suspicious until verified: confirm the NGO on official charity registries before donating, never via forwarded shortlinks.

text: Congratulations! You've won a Dyson V15 in our Diwali Lucky Draw 🎉 You're a valued customer. Just pay Rs 499 shipping to claim: [link]. Offer expires tonight!
safe_action: Treat as suspicious until verified: legitimate prizes never require payment to claim — check the brand's official site.
